site.title: Asahi Suenaga
site.description: I build intuitive open-source software at Michigan State University while studying computer science. I have a sharp eye for detail and I look for perfection in executing my ideas.

about.bio: I'm a computer science major at Michigan State with a curiosity for how things work. I dabble in user interface design and learn Swift in my free time.
about.bioExtra: I build intuitive software to scale big ideas. I believe in algorithms over opinions and testing multiple approaches to find the best fit. As a fast learner with a sharp eye for detail, I look for perfection in executing my ideas.

opensource.title: Open-Source Philosophy
opensource.paragraph1: As a developer, I am constantly making tools for myself, and open-sourcing them is the best way for others facing the same problems to find them.  Instead of letting software sit idle on a private hard drive, sharing it to the public gives a chance for others to learn, fix bugs, and even develop new tools. Whether you’re an individual or an organization, adopting a model of open-sourcing proprietary code showcases practical engineering and builds trust through transparency.
opensource.paragraph2: Developers often adopt open-source programs into their own code from internal utilities to snippets from a retired program. All parties in use of these open resources are responsible for making contributions to the original repository. Contributions range from small donations to creating a fork of the original repository. Everyone on the internet is a recipient of open-source software and a little appreciation gives back to the developers behind the modern internet.
